I think something is fundamentally broken inside the AI labs. Let me explain why.

Look at the builders. Elon in 2008, Tesla and SpaceX both weeks from death, putting his last dollars on the table. Jensen running Nvidia for years under the motto "we're 30 days from going out of business." Travis, kicked out of the company he built with his own hands. Building a company is a machine for humility. Reality hits you every single day. Customers don't care about your vision. Payroll doesn't care about your ego. The market punishes you the moment you start believing your own story. That's why real founders, whatever you think of them, end up grounded. They've been humiliated by reality enough times to know they can be wrong.

Dario's story started well. He left OpenAI at the end of 2020, with a group of researchers, because he didn't like how things were being run there. And on Sam, history proved him right: a board that fired him for not being "consistently candid," the war with Elon over turning a nonprofit into a profit machine, the Scarlett Johansson voice episode. Dario looked at all that and said: not like this. I genuinely believe he was sincere at the start.

But I think he got corrupted by two things.

The first is hubris. Five years from founding to one of the biggest IPOs in history. When the world validates everything you say that fast, you stop hearing the word no. You never get the humbling years Jensen and Elon got.

The second is a deeply collectivist vision of how humanity should be managed. The idea that AI is too dangerous for the many, so a small enlightened group must decide for everyone: who gets chips, which countries, which companies, which models. Jensen summed it up better than anyone: "He thinks AI is so scary, but only they should do it." That's not safety. That's central planning with a moral halo.

Now look at the last two weeks. Jensen goes down in a personal scandal. His private life is his business and his board made its call. But look at who was pushing. Anthropic put $40M into a political group that funded super PACs backing lawmakers who then co-signed the letter demanding Jensen explain himself. The man who stood in the way of chip export bans, the man Trump personally called to tell him to fight for his job, is gone. Days before Anthropic's IPO. And Nvidia is one of Anthropic's investors, which makes the whole thing even stranger.

I'm not saying Dario orchestrated it. Nobody has proven that. But Anthropic and this administration have been at war over AI policy for a long time, and Jensen was the industry's bridge to this White House. When the lab that preaches humility funds the political machine that ends up taking down its biggest ideological opponent, you're allowed to ask questions.

That's the core problem. People who've never been humbled by reality, convinced they're saving humanity, holding the most powerful technology ever built. That's the most dangerous kind of power: the kind that thinks it's virtuous.

Builders build. They don't take down other builders.

x.text:
BofA adds a third hike to its Fed call, now calling for hikes at each of the next three meetings (December, January and March). That’s one more than Goldman, which added a March hike two days ago, and the same path as Deutsche Bank. Unlike Goldman, which sees the first cut in December 2027, BofA has no cuts penciled in for 2027 (or 2028 for that matter).

BofA’s Aditya Bhave (US Economic Weekly) says after October CPI the Fed “no longer has the luxury of hiking at a quarterly pace.” Instead of just pulling March forward, BofA added a hike because “the entire distribution of outcomes has now moved to the right.” BofA also noted Waller’s point that the Fed needs to take back at least last year’s 75 bp of “risk management” cuts. BofA thinks the Fed takes back one of its 2024 cuts too.

Risks both ways, per BofA:
▪️ Downside: “a reflexively dovish committee” could push the last hike to April or June, or skip it, on softer data, a US-Iran deal that pushes oil lower or a sharp equity selloff.
▪️ Upside: a tighter labor market and a jump in wage growth could take rates above 5%, as could another year of big start-of-year price increases.

They still look for 25 bp in December, not 50. BofA says “everything would have to break in favor of the hawks” for a half point, and lists five conditions:

▪️ October core PCE near 0.4% (BofA tracks 0.32%, out November 25).
▪️ November unemployment at 4.0% (October was 4.1%).
▪️ November wage growth of 0.4% (October already hit it).
▪️ More participants, particularly the doves, open to considering 50
▪️ Futures pricing at least a 50% chance of 50 bp (about 14% after CPI).

The debate has shifted from whether the Fed hikes again to how many more times and how fast. Next up are the FOMC minutes Wednesday, which BofA expects to show a deeper split over the October pause than the 10-2 vote suggested.

This is extremely important information: American Medical Doctor reveals how you CAN get the cash price for treatments even if you have insurance

We’ve all seen people asking for the cheaper cash price for treatments but being told no because they have insurance. It turns out you can get the cash price

Under a specific HIPAA Privacy Rule provision (45 CFR § 164.522(a)(1)(vi), added by the HITECH Act), a covered healthcare provider must honor a patient’s request to restrict disclosure of protected health information to their health plan for payment

This gives insured patients a real right to elect self-pay/cash for a service (such as an MRI, CT, or X-ray) and instruct the facility not to bill insurance or share the related information with the insurer for billing purposes

This means that under HIPAA, they MUST honor the cash price for insured patients

Next, if the facility gives you pushback because they won’t risk it with their agreements, that’s fine. There is essentially a fool proof way around this

Let’s say it’s for imaging. You don’t go to a place contracted with a hospital, you go to an independent imaging center and use the HIPAA rule. They aren’t under contract because they’re independent and this Doctor says they will always honor it 

Rules are stricter with Medicare and Medicaid because of mandatory claim submission rules often apply, but for private insurance this is huge

Residents of federally funded public housing will be required to show proof of U.S. citizenship or eligible immigration status under a new rule published Thursday by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development.

The measure could displace nearly 80,000 people, including tens of thousands of citizens in mixed-status families, from their homes, according to the Center for Budget and Policy Priorities, a nonpartisan research and policy institute.

Since 1995, mixed-status families have been permitted to live together in HUD-funded housing as long as federal subsidies covered only eligible household members. The new rule may force these families to decide whether to remain together in nonpublic housing or split up their households.

US layoffs continue to slow sharply:

US job cut announcements dropped -71% YoY in October, to 43,994, the lowest October total since 2023.

Year-to-date announcements have declined -44% YoY, to 617,189, the lowest January-October total since 2022.

This is also the 8th month of 2026 with job cuts down YoY versus the corresponding month of the prior year.

Food companies led October layoffs with 9,677 cuts, while Technology has recorded the most reductions year-to-date, at 171,501, up +21% YoY.

Market and economic conditions accounted for 16,407 announced job cuts in October, or ~37% of all layoffs, bringing the year-to-date total to 130,531, overtaking AI as the most cited reason.

US employers appear to be slowing job cuts.

x.text:
AI Demand Is Real: Prices Halved, Volume Exploded

Skeptics say AI is a capex bubble with no paying customers. The usage data says otherwise.

Weekly token volume on OpenRouter hit 210 trillion last week, up 8% in a single week. A year ago it was in the low single-digit trillions, so volume has grown by a factor of 40 or more in twelve months, and this week is pacing at 215 trillion.

Meanwhile, the price of AI collapsed. Silicon Data’s LLM token expenditure index fell from about $2.00 to about $0.80 per million tokens over the past year, and Anthropic’s weighted price dropped by more than half. When something gets 60% cheaper and usage goes up 40-fold, total spending explodes. That’s Jevons in real time: cheaper compute creates more demand for compute, not less.

The mix is getting heavier too. Memory-intensive long-context requests rose 11% in a week to 616 million. Those are agents, codebases and documents, the workloads that eat GPUs and memory. Proprietary models are holding near $2.00 per million while open models sit at about $0.50, so customers are paying for quality. That’s pricing power, not a race to zero.

This is AI moving from expenditure to evidence. Falling unit costs and exploding volume is the productivity story, the same supply-side force driving unit labour costs lower. The capex is chasing demand that’s already here.

x.name: James E. Thorne
x.text:
Goolsbee Is Driving by the Rear-View Mirror

Goolsbee says inflation is “going the wrong way.” What he’s seeing is an energy shock that’s already over.

Saudi output is back at 10.56mn b/d, up from 6.3mn. WTI has dropped from $102 to the high $ 80s. Tanker rates fell as much as 70% in a week. Add up lower benchmark prices, narrower physical differentials and cheaper freight, and the “landed” cost of oil at the refinery gate is down 35 to 40% since its mid-September peak. That’s a supply shock unwinding, not demand running hot.

Services CPI has been above 2% for 60 years. When the Fed started hiking, services were at 5.1%, and they peaked at 7.6% after the hikes. Core goods came in at 0.16%. The bond market isn’t panicking either: the 5y5y is at 2.17%, below its long-run average.

The progress is coming at the pump and in productivity. Hiking now fights the recovery, not inflation, and Main Street pays the bill.

Why is the Fed acting so irrationally? 

Fed officials pushing for a 50 bp hike say they need it to protect their credibility. The bond market says they never lost it. 

The 5-year, 5-year forward, the gold standard of long-run inflation expectations, is at 2.17%. That’s below its 2.25% average since 2003 and lower than on two-thirds of trading days in that period. It’s also a CPI measure, so in the Fed’s preferred PCE terms it works out to roughly 1.8 to 1.9%, at or below the 2% target. 

Expectations are anchored, and yes,  add the energy shock that’s already fading which will add to disinflationary forces, and the irrationality or incompetence of the Fed is there for the world to see. Wall St problem, no objective research. 

You don’t restore credibility by hiking into a negative supply shock. You lose it by misdiagnosing one. A 50 bp hike would hit Main Street to fix a problem the market says doesn’t exist. The Fed’s credibility isn’t at risk from inflation expectations. It’s at risk from the Fed itself.

US credit stress is intensifying among the weakest-quality borrowers:

Spreads on CCC-rated and lower US corporate bonds are up to 13.3%, near the highest since the 2020 pandemic.

Since January 2026, this figure has surged +490 basis points.

As a result, these spreads have now surpassed the 2022 bear market peak of 12.9%.

For perspective, during the 2020 February-March surge, this metric peaked at 18.8%.

Meanwhile, the spread differential between CCC- and BBB-rated corporate debt has widened to ~1,200 basis points, its widest level in at least 5 years.

This means investors are demanding ~12 percentage points more in compensation to hold the lowest-rated debt rather than first-notch investment-grade corporate bonds.

Cracks are spreading quickly through the lowest-quality credit.

NEWS: Public housing residents will have to prove their citizenship or immigration status under a new HUD rule that could displace tens of thousands of people, per Bloomberg Law.

The rule takes effect Dec 14. It applies to all applicants and current tenants in public housing and Section 8 programs, including vouchers, regardless of age. US citizens will now have to provide documents too, instead of simply declaring citizenship as before.

The rule targets “mixed-status” households, where some members are eligible and others aren’t. Those families have 90 days to submit proof, which can be extended to 150. Their aid becomes temporary while every member’s status is checked. Housing advocates warn families may have to choose between staying together and keeping their assistance.

HUD Secretary Scott Turner says the rule closes a “decades-old loophole” and that “American taxpayers will no longer foot the bill.” HUD says an audit with DHS found nearly 200,000 tenants with incomplete or unknown eligibility records.

Si t'es un prof de gauche, dans 10 ans tu seras au chômage. Pas parce qu'on va te virer. Parce que plus personne ne voudra de toi. Je t'explique pourquoi, et tu vas détester.

Un dressage parfait pour le monde qui attendait les diplômés : le tertiaire, les open spaces, les PowerPoint, le corporate bullshit. On ne vous demandait pas de penser. Un monde a fait sécession avec ça : les startups. Les meilleures boîtes ne recrutent pas des récitants, elles recrutent des libres penseurs. Des gens capables de prendre un savoir et d'en faire quelque chose qui n'existait pas. Parce qu'un problème nouveau, par définition, ça ne se résout pas par cœur. Ça demande de la pensée créative et de la pensée critique. Deux choses que l'école n'a jamais vraiment enseignées.

Et maintenant, l'IA arrive. L'IA est un exécutant parfait. Elle récite mieux que vous. Elle rend la copie attendue mieux que vous. Elle fait le PowerPoint mieux que vous. Tout ce que l'école a passé un siècle à vous apprendre, une machine le fait en trois secondes pour quelques centimes.

Ce qui reste à l'humain ? Penser hors de la boîte. Douter. Contredire. Créer. La synergie homme-IA que tout le monde dessine aujourd'hui ne marche que si l'humain apporte ce que la machine n'a pas : un regard libre.

C'est là que le problème devient explosif. Une grande partie de l'école ne forme plus des esprits libres. Elle forme des croyants. La pensée de gauche, telle qu'elle se pratique dans beaucoup de salles de classe et d'amphis, ne se vit pas comme une opinion parmi d'autres. Elle se vit comme LA vérité. Une doctrine, avec ses dogmes, ses hérétiques, ses mots interdits. Et une doctrine, c'est l'exact inverse de la pensée critique. On ne questionne pas un dogme, on le récite. Je ne suis pas inquiet pour les jeunes. Chassez le naturel, il revient au galop. Small interrogation, empirical edition.

I think I've figured out why some people are absolutely convinced that consciousness is just a byproduct of data. And I keep seeing a correlation that shows up too often to be a coincidence.

Simon Baron-Cohen, one of the leading researchers on autism, distinguishes two main cognitive styles: systemizing and empathizing. The systemizer understands the world by looking for rules, inputs, outputs, mechanisms. The empathizer understands it from the inside, through what it feels like to be someone.

We all have both, in different proportions. Highly systemizing profiles, many of whom are on the autism spectrum, often struggle with anything that doesn't fit in a box.

Think of Sheldon Cooper in The Big Bang Theory. People have to hold up a "sarcasm" sign for him to get it. Sarcasm isn't in the words, it's between the words. And for a mind that runs only on rules, what's between the words is noise.

My hypothesis: consciousness is the ultimate sarcasm. It's precisely the thing that shows up in no dataset. You can measure every neuron, every activation, every token, and you'll never get what it feels like to see red. Chalmers calls it the "hard problem."

So if your mental software consists of fitting everything into a model, the conclusion becomes almost automatic. Whatever isn't in the model doesn't exist, or it "emerges" from complexity. A big enough AI will inevitably become conscious, since consciousness would just be well-organized data.

This isn't just a hunch. A 2012 study (Norenzayan, Gervais, Trzesniewski) found that people who have a harder time representing other people's minds, including autistic people, are on average less likely to believe in a personal God. The results are debated, but the lead is serious.

The most ironic part: many autistic people describe an inner life of incredible intensity. Hypersensitivity to sound, light, textures. In other words, a stronger-than-average subjective experience. The people who most deny consciousness sometimes live it the most intensely, without having a box to put it in.

The problem isn't the cognitive style. It's when it becomes a religion. I was recently talking with a former minister who told me: "Talking to a fundamentalist materialist is like talking to a religious fundamentalist." Same certainty, same dogma, same refusal to admit we don't know.

Because that's the only honest position today: we don't know what consciousness is. Not where it comes from, not whether a machine can have it. Whoever tells you "it's obvious, it's emergent" hasn't solved the problem. 

They've just put it in a box.

x.name: Brivael Le Pogam
x.text:
Mon dernier post disant aux jeunes de ne pas faire d'études a fait réagir. Je précise.

Je ne suis pas contre l'éducation. Je pense que c'est la chose la plus noble qui existe. Je crois profondément au rôle du professeur.

Je déconseille de faire des études pour une raison simple : l'école aujourd'hui n'est plus un outil d'éducation. C'est un outil d'endoctrinement.

Revenons à ce que l'éducation était censée être. Socrate, le père de la philosophie occidentale, résumait toute sa sagesse en une phrase : je sais que je ne sais rien. Le point de départ de toute pensée, c'est le doute. Montaigne voulait une tête bien faite plutôt que bien pleine. Plutarque disait que l'esprit n'est pas un vase qu'on remplit, mais un feu qu'on allume. Kant définissait les Lumières comme la sortie de l'homme de sa minorité : ose penser par toi-même. Et Nietzsche avertissait qu'on récompense mal un maître si l'on reste toujours son élève.

Tout est là. Le rôle de l'école, c'est de vous apprendre à apprendre. De vous apprendre à douter. Y compris de ce qu'on vous enseigne. Un vrai prof devrait vous donner les outils pour critiquer son propre cours.

Aujourd'hui, c'est l'inverse. En grande majorité, l'école est devenue une machine à faire ingurgiter, à formater, à dire ce qu'il faut penser. Wokisme, anticapitalisme, décroissance : on ne vous présente pas ces idées pour les discuter, on vous les installe comme des évidences. Et quiconque les questionne devient suspect.

Le résultat, je le vois tous les jours. Beaucoup de jeunes sont totalement bloqués mentalement. Incapables d'avoir une pensée créative. Pas parce qu'ils sont moins intelligents que les générations d'avant. Parce qu'ils se sont fait broyer par le système.

Attention, ce sont souvent d'excellents exécutants. Bosseurs, rigoureux, capables de rendre exactement ce qu'on attend d'eux. Mais derrière, il y a une pensée dogmatique absolument terrifiante. Des certitudes qu'ils n'ont jamais examinées. Des opinions dont ils ignorent l'origine. Ils ne savent pas pourquoi ils pensent ce qu'ils pensent.

Et à l'ère de l'IA, c'est le pire profil possible. L'exécution scolaire, la machine le fait déjà mieux que vous. Ce qui restera rare, c'est la capacité à penser contre, à douter, à créer.

Ce système ne se réformera pas à la marge. Il devra être complètement reset. Et ça passera par une étape primordiale : la dégauchisation de l'université et du corps enseignant. Pas pour remplacer une idéologie par une autre. Pour revenir au rôle essentiel de l'éducation : la pensée critique, la capacité à remettre en question l'autorité, et apprendre à apprendre.

Ce jour-là, on reviendra aux humanités. À l'art. À la philosophie. Aux profs comme mentors, pas comme prêcheurs. À une éducation qui forme des esprits libres plutôt que des esprits conformes.

En attendant, si vous avez 18 ans, ne confiez pas votre cerveau à un système qui veut le formater. Lisez les philosophes. Doutez de tout, y compris de moi. Et construisez.

x.name: Brivael Le Pogam
x.text:
Des jeunes me demandent souvent s'ils doivent faire des études.

Laurent Alexandre leur déconseille les études, sauf les grandes écoles.

Moi, je vais plus loin. Ne faites pas d'études. Point.

Je parle souvent de la gauche. Mais je n'avais pas mesuré à quel point, en 15-20 ans, l'école est devenue une machine d'endoctrinement. Wokisme, anticapitalisme, décroissance, marxisme : l'idéologie n'est pas juste entrée dans le système. Elle l'a capturé.

Tu rentres avec l'envie de construire. Tu ressors convaincu que la croissance détruit la planète, que l'entreprise c'est de l'exploitation, que l'ambition est suspecte. Le système même qui a créé toute l'abondance autour de toi, on t'apprend à le détester.

Et le pire, ce n'est même pas l'idéologie. C'est qu'en détruisant l'esprit critique, l'école fabrique des gens incapables de penser. Ils ont des opinions, mais ils ne savent pas pourquoi ils les ont. Ils ne les ont jamais questionnées. Ils les ont juste absorbées.

C'est absolument catastrophique. Une société où les gens ne savent pas pourquoi ils pensent ce qu'ils pensent, c'est une société qu'on peut emmener n'importe où.

Aujourd'hui, la fac et les écoles d'ingé sont en grande majorité des broyeurs de pensée créative. On vous y apprend à exécuter de manière scolaire. Suivre les consignes, réciter, rentrer dans le moule.

Il n'y a plus de place pour ces profils. L'IA fait ça mieux, plus vite, moins cher.

Donc si vous avez 18 ans, un peu de jugeote et la dalle :

→ Montez votre boîte maintenant. Ou allez bosser dans une startup avec des founders qui vous inspirent.

→ Intéressez-vous à la philosophie. Développez votre esprit critique. Apprenez à penser, pas à réciter.

→ Construisez des choses par vous-même.

Mais ne vous laissez surtout pas brainwasher.

x.name: Krakenmiller
x.text:
[생각정리]

크립토 불장이 언제 올 지는 모르겠습니다.

그렇지만 누군가 불장이 2년내로 올거냐고 물어본다면 그렇다고 대답할 거 같습니다.

솔직하게 말씀드리자면, 26년 큰 상승을 기대했었습니다.

현재까지 봤을땐 명백히 틀렸습니다.

하지만 괜찮습니다.

올해가 아니라면 내년, 내년이 아니라면 내후년까지는 올 거 같거든요.

제가 크립토에 투자하는 이유는 명확합니다.

미국 정부가 스테이블 코인을 원한다.

월스트리트를 포함한 전통금융이 온체인으로 올라오고 있다. 생각보다 더 빠른 속도로.

AI에이전트 시대가 오고 있으며, 그들의 경제활동엔 크립토가 필요하다.

크립토 산업의 성장에는 의구심이 없으며 다가올 미래이자 진행중인 현재라고 생각합니다.

다만 의문이 드는 건 산업의 성장과 크립토 시장 펌핑이 연결되느냐 입니다.

저는 이 질문에는 아니라고 대답하고 싶습니다.

장기적으로 산업의 성장과 토큰의 가치가 연결되지는 않다고 봅니다.

HYPE 같은 일부 연결되는 코인들이 존재합니다만, 현존하는 대부분의 코인은 그 연결고리가 끊겨있다고 봅니다.

그럼에도 코인(특히 알트코인)을 가지고 있는 건 온체인금융으로의 이동이라는 내터리브가 너무나 매력적이기 때문입니다.

저는 이 매력적인 내러티브가 광기장을 만드는 날이 분명 올 거라고 봅니다.

특히 그간의 코인시장을 봤을때 이 내러티브를 안쓰고 이대로 사라지는건 상상이 잘 가지 않거든요.

그래서 저는 극히 일부의 코인을 제외하고는 투기적으로 접근하는 게 맞다고 보고 저 역시 투기적으로 보고있습니다.

그러면 왜 2년내로 상승할 것이라고 생각하냐.

사실 잘풀리면 내년초부터 상승장이 시작할거라고 봅니다.

코인시장이 불장이 되려면 결국 유동성이 뒷받침 되어야 합니다.

세상에서 존재하는 자산군중에서 제일 늦게 돈이 도달하는 곳이거든요.

저는 풍부한 유동성과 코인을 사야하는 이유가 만들어져야 불장이 온다고 생각하거든요?

내년엔 그런 환경이 조성될 가능성이 있습니다.

종전, 유동성, 제도화.

위 3가지가 내년에 모두 충족될 가능성이 꽤 있다고 생각합니다.

1. 종전

이미 공화당이 중간선거에서 참패하면서 이란과의 전쟁을 끌고가기 힘들어졌습니다.

특히 전쟁으로 인한 고유가가 선거에서 발목을 잡았습니다.

지금 이미 협상중이며, 이르면 올해 늦어도 내년까지는 끝날 것으로 예상합니다.

내후년엔 대선이 있기에 그때까지 끌고 가는 건 정치적으로 큰 부담입니다.

게다가 러-우 전쟁 종전 가능성도 요근래 많이 올라왔다고 봅니다.

내년엔 두 개의 전쟁이 끝날 가능성이 있습니다.

2. 유동성

현재 유동성이 그리 좋은 편은 아니라고 생각합니다.

금리인상이 시작됐고, 12월엔 추가 금리인상이 예고되어 있습니다.

내년에도 1-2차례 금리 인상한다는 게 시장 컨센이고요.

현재 미국 10년물이 5% 넘게 찍히고 있으며,

빅테크들이 발행하는 채권 역시 금리가 높습니다.

현금이 비싼 시대라고 보고, 시중에 여유돈이 넉넉한 상황은 아니라고 생각합니다.

크립토에 돈이 들어오려면 결국 여유돈이 시중에 좀 있어줘야 합니다.

저는 내년에는 그런 환경이 만들어질 가능성이 있다고 보고 있습니다.

현재 재무부가 TGA잔고를 높은 수준으로 유지하고 있습니다.

현재 부채한도 41조달러인데, 부채한도가 거의 다 찼으며 민주당이 중간선거 대승하면서 한도 협상하기가 더 힘들어졌다고 생각합니다.

부채한도에 도달해 신규 순차입이 제한되면, 재무부는 특별조치와 함께 TGA 잔고를 활용해 자금 집행을 이어갈 수 있습니다. 이 과정에서 TGA가 감소하면 시중 유동성에 긍정적으로 작용할 수 있습니다.

25년 8월에 이더리움이 ATH를 달성했을 때를 보겠습니다.

25년 2월에 TGA잔고가 8,300억 달러 수준이었는데 25년 7월말 3,000억 달러 수준까지 빠졌습니다.

물론 저는 그당시 제일 중요한 건 지니어스액트라고 생각합니다만, 유동성이 뒷받침 된 것도 사실입니다.

25년 10월 8,000억달러까지 올라온 이후 1년이 넘는 기간동안 TGA잔고가 현재 레벨(8,000억 ~ 1조 달러)를 유지하고 있으며, 부채한도가 꽉차고 협상이 지속되는 기간 TGA잔고가 낮은 레벨로 내려가주는 모습을 기대하고 있습니다.

그리고 1번과 연결해보겠습니다.

내년까지 금리인상이 2~3회정도 예상되어 있지만 저는 다른 그림을 좀 그려보고 싶습니다.

전쟁이 끝나고 유가가 잡히면서 끈적했던 물가가 내려가는 모습이 나올 가능성을 열어두고 있습니다.

워시가 그린스펀을 언급하기도 했고, 워시 역시 AI 생산성이 결국 디스인플레이션을 만들거라고 주장했습니다.

AI 생산성 향상과 에너지 가격 안정이 인플레이션 압력을 완화한다면, 시장이 예상하는 것보다 Fed의 긴축 기조가 빠르게 전환될 가능성도 열어두고 있습니다.

3. 제도화

저는 이부분이 제일 크다고 생각합니다.

24년 11월 트럼프 당선 이후의 불장, 25년 8월 이더리움 ATH 그리고 이번 26년 8월의 반등까지.

모두 제도화와 연결되어 있다고 생각합니다.

24년 11월은 "미국을 암호화폐 수도로 만들겠다"는 트럼프 당선으로 시작된 상승이었고

25년 8월은 지니어스 액트 통과로 인한 상승이라고 봅니다.

또한 이번 26년 8월의 반등을 이유를 베센트의 장기채매입 발언으로 보는 의견도 있지만,

저는 SEC의 Regulation Crypto Assets 초안 공개가 반등의 이유라고 봅니다.

따라서 제도화가 크립토에서는 제일 중요하다고 보고있습니다.

27년엔 제도화에 대한 기대감이 큽니다.

먼저 클래리티 액트.

민주당의 반대로 무산됐지만, 중간선거가 끝났으니 저는 달라질 수 있다고 봅니다.

선거가 없는 27년도기에 정치적인 부담이 좀 덜어진 상태이고, 민주당을 후원하는 월가의 주요 플레이어들(특히 은행들)은 클래리티를 원합니다. 예금이 스테이블코인으로 유출되기를 원하지 않거든요.

은행위원장에 워런이 앉을 것으로 유력한 게 많이 걸리지만, 양당 모두 디지털자산 시장의 규제 명확성이 필요하다는 데에는 일정 부분 공감대가 있다고 생각합니다. 다만 윤리조항과 스테이블코인 보상 문제에서 이견이 남아 있는 만큼, 중간선거 이후 협상 환경이 어떻게 바뀌는지가 중요할 것 같습니다.

만약 클래리티가 안된다면요?

대안이 기다립니다.

8월에 공개된 Regulation Crypto Assets이 공개의견 수렴 기간이 끝났습니다.

법안을 다듬고, 내년초쯤 최종안이 나오고 규칙으로 제정될 것이라고 봅니다.

Regulation Crypto Assets만이 끝이 아닙니다.

SEC와 CFTC의 움직임을 보면 크립토에 굉장히 우호적이며 규칙으로 제정하고자 하는 모습이 보입니다.

법률만큼 안정적인 제도적 기반은 아니겠지만, 최종 규칙이 마련된다면 기관들이 크립토 시장에 진입할 때 고려할 수 있는 중요한 규제적 근거가 될 것이라고 생각합니다.

또한 2027년 1월부터 GENIUS Act가 본격적으로 시행됩니다.

GENIUS Act가 시행되면 은행을 비롯한 전통 금융기관들이 명확한 규제체계 아래 스테이블코인 사업에 진출할 수 있는 기반이 마련됩니다.

저는 이 변화가 상당히 중요하다고 생각합니다.

그동안 스테이블코인은 주로 크립토 시장 내부에서 활용되어 왔지만, 앞으로는 전통 금융기관의 결제와 송금, 토큰화 자산의 정산 등으로 활용 범위가 확대될 가능성이 있기 때문입니다.

즉, 기존 금융시스템에서 이동하던 달러가 블록체인 위에서도 이동하기 시작하는 것입니다.

물론 이것이 곧바로 모든 코인의 가격 상승을 의미하지는 않습니다.

하지만 스테이블코인이 전통 금융과 온체인 금융을 연결하는 핵심 인프라로 자리 잡는다면, 온체인 금융으로의 이동은 단순한 내러티브가 아니라 실제 금융산업의 변화로 이어질 수 있다고 생각합니다.

저는 2027년이 2026년보다 크립토 시장에 더 우호적인 해가 될 가능성이 있다고 생각합니다.

전쟁이 끝나고 유가가 안정되면서 금융여건이 개선되고, 동시에 크립토 제도화가 진전되는 그림을 기대하고 있습니다.

물론 이 모든 조건이 충족된다는 보장은 없습니다.

그리고 온체인 금융산업이 성장한다고 해서 모든 코인이 상승할 것이라고 생각하지도 않습니다.

Bitcoin has been getting crushed in Q4, and Jane Street's latest SEC filings reveal something interesting.

Just before the Q4 selloff began, Jane Street was aggressively increasing its Bitcoin ETF exposure.

During Q3:

• Fidelity Bitcoin ETF holdings jumped from 887K to 7.01 MILLION shares, worth $509 MILLION.

• BlackRock Bitcoin ETF holdings were worth another $957 MILLION.

• ARK Bitcoin ETF holdings reached around $249 MILLION.

By September 30, Jane Street held roughly $1.7 BILLION across these three Bitcoin ETFs.

Then Q4 began, and Bitcoin started getting hammered.

But the strange part is when the selling has been happening.

BTC has repeatedly faced heavy selling pressure around the U.S. stock market open.

At the same time, the Coinbase premium has remained negative since late September.

Even when buying appeared on other exchanges, Bitcoin continued trading at a discount on Coinbase.

This shows persistent weakness in U.S. spot demand.

Now remember Jane Street's history.

In July 2025, India's market regulator took action against Jane Street over a strategy involving large stock purchases, bearish options positions and aggressive selling. SEBI identified around $567 MILLION in alleged unlawful gains.

Then, in February 2026, Jane Street faced a lawsuit over its trading during the Terra collapse.

There was also daily 10 AM selling pattern, which stopped after was sued by Tera.

Now look at what we're seeing again.

Jane Street built substantial Bitcoin ETF exposure in Q3.

Bitcoin started dumping repeatedly during U.S. trading hours in Q4.

Buying Bitcoin ETFs doesn't mean a trading firm is betting on higher prices.

It can hold those ETFs while taking much larger short positions through futures or options.

If Bitcoin falls, profits from those shorts can offset losses on the ETF holdings.

And if the short exposure is large enough, the firm could make money even during a major Bitcoin crash.

SO WAS JANE STREET ACTUALLY BULLISH ON BITCOIN IN Q3, OR WAS IT BUILDING ONE SIDE OF A MUCH BIGGER TRADE?

Its SEC filings show the ETF positions, but they don't reveal its full derivatives exposure during Q4.

There is no direct evidence connecting Jane Street to the recent Bitcoin dumps.

But given its previous trading controversies, the real question is whether Jane Street was also positioned to profit while Bitcoin was getting destroyed.

x.text:
🚨 Another major scandal is coming out of NVIDIA.

And this one has nothing to do with Jensen Huang's affairs.

According to a Wall Street Journal report, Nvidia was offering billions in financial guarantees to AI companies that could not afford its chips, so they could keep buying them.

Some of these deals were being pushed by Jensen's own son-in-law, Nico Caprez, who became a vice president in January. His team was telling small cloud companies and data center builders that Nvidia could arrange credit support for them within a couple of weeks.

The goal was simple: turn them into long term buyers of Nvidia GPUs.

And the size of Nvidia's commitments has exploded. Its own filing shows $530 BILLION in commitments and guarantees, up from $184 billion just one quarter earlier.

Inside the company, CFO Colette Kress was raising concerns. She kept asking how these guarantees were priced and what Nvidia was really getting back.

In an August meeting, Jensen cut her off and called her "a deer in the headlights."

She was also the one who cut Nvidia's guarantee on OpenAI's Ohio data center from $250 billion to $105 billion.

Now Jensen is gone, and the CFO who questioned these deals is running Nvidia.

To understand why this is a big deal, you need to understand the AI funding loop.

Here is how it works:

1. Nvidia puts money into an AI company, or guarantees its loans and leases.
2. That company uses the money and credit to build a data center.
3. The data center is filled with Nvidia GPUs.
4. Nvidia reports those GPU sales as revenue.
5. If the company cannot rent out all its computing power, Nvidia agrees to buy the unused part.

SO NVIDIA IS THE INVESTOR, THE LENDER, THE SUPPLIER AND THE BACKUP CUSTOMER, ALL IN THE SAME DEAL.

The money goes out of Nvidia and comes back to Nvidia as sales.

CoreWeave is the clearest example. Nvidia owns a stake in it, sells it chips, and agreed to buy up to $6.3 billion of its unused computing capacity through 2032.

OpenAI is the biggest. Nvidia is guaranteeing up to $105 billion for its Ohio data center, supplying all the chips inside it, and invested $1.5 billion in the company building it.

Nvidia's own filing for the quarter ending July 26 shows where the money is tied up:

• Supply commitments for memory and chip wafers: $279 BILLION, up from $119 billion.
• Guarantee on the OpenAI Ohio data center: up to $105 BILLION.
• Deals to buy unused cloud capacity from neoclouds: $36 BILLION.

Nvidia's actual liabilities on its balance sheet: $91 BILLION.

That means the commitments outside the balance sheet are almost 6 times bigger than the debts on it.

Nvidia does not lose this money unless something breaks. A guarantee only costs Nvidia if a customer cannot pay.

But this is where it gets uncomfortable.

The WSJ says Jensen himself had started to panic. He warned executives that the biggest cloud companies were moving to their own chips to depend less on Nvidia.

At the same time, the wafers and memory Nvidia had committed to buy were coming at him like an "avalanche."

So the biggest customers were trying to leave, Nvidia was locked into buying huge amounts of supply, and smaller customers were being kept alive with Nvidia's credit.

And things were already starting to crack:

• Nvidia paused some of its financing deals in August.
• Nearly half of the $80 billion in data center bonds issued this year were rated junk.
• Neocloud stocks crashed this week, with Nebius down over 20% and CoreWeave down 17% at the lows.
• OpenAI raised less than it wanted, at a lower valuation.

And now Kress is the one deciding whether this continues.

If she pulls back on the financing, the companies that depended on Nvidia's money will have to borrow elsewhere, in a debt market that is already nervous.

If they cannot, they stop buying chips.

And if they stop buying chips, Nvidia's revenue drops.

That is the risk of a loop. It works perfectly when money keeps flowing, and it hurts on the way down.

CONTEXT: On August 2, 2026, THE WASHINGTON POST published an investigation examining how police officers across America had abused automated license-plate recognition systems.

The newspaper initially identified AT LEAST 50 LAW ENFORCEMENT OFFICERS who had been charged with or accused of improperly accessing these surveillance networks.

THEIR GIRLFRIENDS.
THEIR EX-GIRLFRIENDS.
THEIR WIVES.
THEIR EXES' NEW ROMANTIC PARTNERS.

FLOCK'S TECHNOLOGY WAS INVOLVED IN 46 OF THE 50 CASES.

By AUGUST 19, The Washington Post had identified AT LEAST 69 POLICE OFFICIALS accused, charged or convicted of unauthorized license-plate-reader use.

But here's what makes this technology so powerful.

According to Flock, its network has grown to approximately 120,000 CAMERAS across 49 STATES, generating roughly 20 BILLION LICENSE-PLATE SCANS EVERY MONTH.

These aren't ordinary traffic cameras that only activate when you run a red light.

They can automatically record a passing vehicle's LICENSE PLATE, location, time, make, model and other identifying details.

Authorized law enforcement users can then search the resulting database to locate vehicles and reconstruct patterns of movement.

And that's where Rogan's concern becomes particularly serious.

Imagine an officer who becomes obsessed with a woman he met at the gym.

He knows what car she drives.

He searches her license plate.

If enough camera detections are available, he may be able to establish where her car regularly appears.

WHERE SHE WORKS.

WHERE SHE SPENDS HER EVENINGS.

AND POTENTIALLY WHERE SHE LIVES.

x.name: James E. Thorne
x.text:
The Cycle Isn’t Over. Demand for Intelligence Has No Human Ceiling

Every past tech cycle ended for the same reason: demand ran out of people. There were only so many households to buy a PC, so many users to get online and so many people to carry a smartphone. Once adoption saturated, capacity caught up, prices broke and the cycle turned.

AI breaks that pattern. Demand for intelligence isn’t capped by human headcount, because machines consume it too. AI agents call other agents, models generate their own training data, and reasoning models burn many times more tokens on every query. Each gain in efficiency becomes more consumption, not spare capacity.

The data shows it:

•  H100 rents are at a record: renting a previous-generation H100 now costs $3.10 an hour, up 56% in a year. In a normal cycle, legacy chips get cheaper as new chips arrive. Blackwell is shipping, yet the H100 still isn’t obsolete, and it’s earning more.

•  Usage is compounding: token volume is up about 40-fold in a year, even as the price per token fell from about $2.00 to $0.80.

•  Inventories are thin: memory makers hold under 10 days of supply.

A cycle ends when supply overtakes demand. Rising prices for old hardware tell you supply is still chasing demand. Wall st. can argue about multiples, but the earnings cycle isn’t over.

x.name: Brivael Le Pogam
x.text:
Je viens de regarder mon passage dans Quotidien. Évidemment, je suis qualifié d’« influenceur entrepreneur d’extrême droite ».

Déroulons.

Je ne sais pas si vous vous rendez compte à quel point le peuple français vous méprise.

Vous êtes tellement déconnectés du réel que, dans votre petit monde, vous êtes persuadés d’avoir le monopole du bon sens. Alors je vais vous dire ce que vous êtes vraiment. Mais avant, je vais vous dire d’où je parle.

Je suis breton. J’ai grandi dans un système scolaire profondément cassé. La majorité de mes profs étaient de gauche, et la plupart étaient déprimés. Pas méchants. Déprimés. Ils ne transmettaient qu’une chose : la conviction que le monde est injuste, que l’effort ne paie pas, et que demain sera pire qu’hier.

Ce qui m’a sauvé, c’est d’avoir appris seul. J’ai commencé à coder à 12 ans. À 15 ans, j’avais créé un jeu qui me rapportait plus que le salaire de mes profs. Personne ne m’a donné la permission. Personne ne m’a subventionné. J’ai construit, des gens ont joué, j’ai été payé. La leçon d’économie la plus honnête de ma vie.

Ensuite j’ai travaillé dans la tech, j’ai vécu dans la Silicon Valley, j’ai construit pas mal de choses. Et j’ai étudié l’économie par moi-même. Pas pour un diplôme. Pour comprendre comment le monde fonctionne vraiment.

Et surtout, j’ai eu une chance que vous n’aurez jamais. J’ai été connecté, et je le suis encore, aux deux extrémités de la société. D’un côté, les couches les plus modestes, celles que vous prétendez protéger et incarner sans jamais leur parler. De l’autre, les couches les plus hautes : des milliardaires, des bâtisseurs, Elon Musk. Je fais le grand écart tous les jours. Et je peux vous dire une chose : en bas comme en haut, le diagnostic est le même. Vous, vous êtes au milieu, dans le seul étage de l’immeuble qui n’a pas de fenêtre.

Ce que je vais dire maintenant, n’importe quelle personne saine d’esprit qui a un contact avec le réel le comprend.

Yann, tu incarnes un mouvement et des idées qui ne représentent quasiment plus que vous. Ceux qui croient encore Quotidien et ses mensonges répétés en boucle, ce sont deux populations. Les gamins endoctrinés par une école capturée par l’idéologie. Et une partie des Français issus de l’immigration, qu’on manipule en leur répétant que les Français sont racistes. Un récit construit de toutes pièces par cette gauche mortifère, qui a besoin de victimes pour exister et qui les enferme dans ce rôle pour garder leurs voix.

Les idées que vous défendez sont des idées de mort. Elles culpabilisent le travail. Elles humilient ceux qui construisent. Elles transforment chaque citoyen en assisté ou en suspect. Partout où elles ont été appliquées jusqu’au bout, elles ont produit la même chose : la pauvreté, la défiance, l’effondrement. Pas une exception. Pas une.

Je le dis souvent : dans votre camp, il y a les cyniques et les believers. Les cyniques savent que ça ne marche pas, mais ça leur rapporte de l’audience, du pouvoir, des subventions. Les believers, eux, y croient sincèrement.

Yann, je vais te laisser le bénéfice du doute. Je te range dans la case des believers. Alors un conseil : lis Hayek. La Route de la servitude. Ça se lit en un week-end, et ça t’expliquera pourquoi chaque bonne intention que tu défends à l’antenne pave exactement la route que tu prétends combattre.

Tu as sans doute l’impression d’être du bon côté de l’histoire. Ils l’avaient tous. Mais tout ce que tu représentes enverra la France dans le chaos total.

Les gens que tu appelles « extrême droite », ce sont des gens normaux. Des gens qui veulent vivre en sécurité, travailler, être payés dignement pour ce qu’ils font, et élever leur famille dans un pays qu’ils reconnaissent encore. C’est tout. Ce n’est pas une idéologie. C’est le bon sens que vous avez abandonné, puis insulté.

Et je ne sais pas si vous mesurez ce qui est en train de se passer. Les peuples, dans leur intégralité, et avec eux les entrepreneurs, les créateurs de valeur, tous ceux qui font tourner ce pays, commencent à vous détester. Pas à vous critiquer. À vous détester, profondément, viscéralement. Chaque leçon de morale, chaque étiquette, chaque sketch condescendant creuse un peu plus le fossé. Alors un conseil d’ami : calmez-vous. Vraiment.

Je viens d’un milieu très loin des salons feutrés parisiens et des dîners bobos où l’on décide entre soi qui a le droit de parler. Toi, tu vis dans une bulle. Une bulle confortable, chauffée, avec un public qui rit au signal.

Mais le réel ne rit pas au signal.

Plus personne ne vous croit. Et le réel vous jugera. Très sévèrement.

그 배우는 바로 키아누 리브스임

2. 왜냐하면, 키아누 리브스는 다정한 말투와 주변 사람을 위하는 행동으로 유명한 배우이기 때문임

3. 영화 매트릭스를 찍을때도 그가 같이 고생했던 스턴트맨들에게 돌렸던 선물이 화제가 된적이 있었음

4. 영화 ‘매트릭스 리로디드’에 네오가 수많은 스미스 요원과 싸우는 장면이 있음
화면에서는 같은 얼굴이 끝없이 몰려오는데, 실제 촬영에서는 스턴트맨들이 키아누와 동작을 맞추고 바닥에 떨어지는 일을 반복해야 했음

5. 키아누가 인터뷰에서 설명했는데, 이 씬을 찍기 위한 준비 기간만 약 3주, 촬영은 거의 한 달이었음
며칠 연습하고 한 번 멋있게 찍은 장면이 아니라, 같은 사람들끼리 몸을 맞대며 몇 주씩 만들어낸 액션이었던 거

6. 특히 네오가 두 요원에게 붙잡혔다가 뒤로 돌면서 발차기하는 동작이 있었음
키아누에 따르면 그 장면에서 스턴트맨들이 바닥에 내던져진 횟수가 21번이었다고 함
본인이 한 번 더 하고 싶다고 할 때마다 그쪽에서도 다시 하자고 받아줬다는 거임

7. 촬영이 끝난 뒤 키아누는 함께한 스턴트맨 12명에게 할리데이비슨 새 오토바이를 한 대씩 선물함
자기도 오토바이를 좋아하는 배우인데, 동료들한테도 그걸 통째로 돌린 거

8. 이게 본인이 인터뷰 시작하자마자 자랑한 일도 아니었음 
시네마투데이의 당시 인터뷰에 따르면 함께 출연한 제이다 핀켓 스미스가 홍보 과정에서 먼저 이야기했고, 이후 키아누가 선물을 준 이유를 설명함

9. 키아누의 설명은 이거였음
다 같이 훈련했고 다 같이 장면을 만들었으니, 그냥 ‘고맙다’는 말 말고 좀 더 크게 고마움을 전하고 싶었다는 것.
본인이 생각하는 멋진 영화 속 싸움을 만들도록 도와준 사람들에게 준 선물이었던 거임

10. 더 웃긴건 선물하고 나서는 몇 달 동안 그 생각만 해도 웃음이 났다고 함
잠자리에 누워서도 떠올리며 웃었다고 당시 인터뷰에서 이야기함 ㅋㅋ
받는 사람만 좋아한 게 아니라 준 사람도 계속 신났던 거

키아누 리브스는 영화배우로서 얼마나 많은 돈을 버는지에 대해서 항상 부끄러워 한다고 말해서 화제가 된적 있음
그 때문에 동료와 가족 그리고 다른 사람들에게 후한 선물을 아낌없이 베푸는 걸로 유명함

우리가 기억하는 건 네오 혼자 싸우는 장면인데, 키아누가 촬영 끝나고 챙긴 건 그 장면에서 같이 넘어지고 다시 일어난 사람들이었음

TRON, 블록체인을 넘어 일상과 실물경제를 연결하는 범용 인프라
@trondao @TronDao_KOR

블록체인의 경쟁력은 더 이상 얼마나 많은 기술을 보유하고 있느냐만으로 결정되지 않습니다. 얼마나 많은 사람이 실제로 사용하고, 얼마나 자연스럽게 일상에 녹아들 수 있느냐가 중요한 기준이 되고 있습니다.

그런 관점에서 TRON의 최근 성장세는 상당히 의미가 있습니다.

3분기 동안 TRON에는 하루 평균 178,641개의 신규 주소가 추가됐으며, 전체 계정 수는 약 4억 1,400만 개에 도달했습니다. 단순히 숫자가 늘어났다는 의미를 넘어 TRON이 글로벌 디지털 경제에서 실제 사용자를 확보하고 있다는 점에 주목할 필요가 있습니다.

특히 TRON의 강점은 범용성입니다.

블록체인은 과거 특정 투자자나 기술에 익숙한 사람들만 이용하는 영역에 가까웠습니다. 하지만 이제는 송금, 결제, 자산 이동처럼 누구나 일상에서 필요로 하는 기능으로 활용 범위가 넓어지고 있습니다.

TRON은 이러한 변화의 중심에서 스테이블코인 기반 금융 활동을 뒷받침하고 있습니다. 국경을 넘어 자산을 전송하고, 복잡한 중개 과정 없이 디지털 달러를 이동시키는 경험은 기존 금융 시스템이 가진 시간과 비용의 제약을 줄여줍니다.

여기에 편리한 접근성을 더하는 것이 Mercuryo Swaps와 같은 서비스입니다.

TRON 생태계에 자산을 입금하거나 출금하는 과정에서 하나의 인터페이스를 통해 스왑을 진행하고, 거래 전에 최종 수령 금액을 확인할 수 있다는 점은 사용자 경험 측면에서 중요합니다. 거래 도중 예상하지 못한 금액 변동을 걱정해야 하는 불편함을 줄여주기 때문입니다.

기술이 아무리 뛰어나더라도 사용 과정이 복잡하다면 대중화에는 한계가 있습니다. 반대로 사용자가 블록체인이라는 사실을 의식하지 않아도 원하는 자산을 편리하게 이동하고 사용할 수 있다면 이야기는 달라집니다.

TRON이 추구하는 방향도 결국 이런 자연스러운 금융 경험에 있다고 생각합니다.

더 나아가 주목해야 할 분야는 RWA입니다.

부동산, 채권, 주식, 원자재와 같은 현실 세계의 자산이 토큰화되면 블록체인은 단순한 가상자산 거래 공간을 넘어 실물경제와 연결되는 금융 인프라로 확장될 수 있습니다.

토큰화된 자산을 더 빠르게 이동시키고, 스테이블코인을 활용해 결제하며, 다양한 금융 서비스와 연결하는 구조가 만들어진다면 TRON의 역할도 더욱 커질 수 있습니다.

특히 RWA가 성장하기 위해서는 안정적인 결제 수단과 낮은 거래 비용, 빠른 처리 속도, 폭넓은 접근성이 중요합니다. TRON이 그동안 스테이블코인과 글로벌 결제 영역에서 쌓아온 경험은 이러한 시장 변화에 대응할 수 있는 중요한 기반입니다.

결국 TRON의 미래를 단순히 계정 수나 거래량만으로 평가해서는 안 됩니다.

4억 개가 넘는 계정이라는 규모 뒤에는 자산을 이동시키는 사람들, 디지털 금융을 이용하는 사용자들, 그리고 새로운 서비스를 만들어가는 생태계 참여자들이 있습니다.

블록체인이 특별한 기술에서 누구나 사용하는 일상적인 인프라로 변화하는 과정.

송금과 결제에서 시작해 DeFi와 RWA, 나아가 실물경제 전반으로 연결되는 과정에서 TRON은 점점 더 중요한 역할을 할 가능성이 있습니다.

기술을 사용하는 시대에서 기술이 일상에 자연스럽게 스며드는 시대로.

TRON의 진정한 경쟁력은 바로 그 접점을 얼마나 넓혀가느냐에 달려 있습니다.

@trondao @TronDao_KOR

양-밀 이론, 그리고 수학이 도전하는 마지막 문턱

우리는 보이지 않는다고 해서 존재하지 않는다고 말할 수 없습니다.

1편에서 살펴본 무리수가 그랬습니다. √2와 π는 분수로 정확하게 표현할 수 없지만 분명히 존재합니다. 칸토어는 대각선 논법을 통해 실수와 무리수의 세계가 자연수처럼 하나씩 셀 수 없는 구조라는 사실도 증명했습니다.

2편에서는 무한에도 서로 다른 크기가 있다는 것을 살펴봤습니다. 끝이 없다는 하나의 표현 안에도 우리가 직관적으로 이해하기 어려운 수학적 구조가 존재했습니다.

그리고 3편부터는 시선을 자연의 세계로 옮겼습니다.

양-밀 이론은 눈에 보이지 않는 입자와 힘의 상호작용을 설명하는 중요한 수학적 틀입니다. 특히 강한 상호작용을 설명하는 양자색역학의 기반이 되는 이론이기도 합니다.

하지만 이론이 물리학적으로 유용하다는 것과 그 수학적 구조가 엄밀하게 존재한다는 사실은 다릅니다.

여기서 등장하는 것이 저스틴 선 어워드 6번 문제, 양-밀 이론의 존재성과 질량 간극입니다.

이 문제는 4차원 시공간에서 비자명한 양-밀 양자장론을 수학적으로 엄밀하게 구성하고, 그 이론에 양의 질량 간극이 존재한다는 사실을 증명할 것을 요구합니다.

그런데 이제 이 과정에 AI가 참여하기 시작했습니다.

AI는 방대한 수학적 자료를 분석하고, 복잡한 계산을 수행하며, 인간이 쉽게 발견하지 못하는 패턴과 관계를 찾아낼 수 있습니다. 특히 양-밀 이론처럼 여러 수학 분야가 복잡하게 얽혀 있는 문제에서는 새로운 접근법을 탐색하는 데 도움을 줄 수 있습니다.

하지만 여기에는 중요한 차이가 있습니다.

AI가 어떤 규칙을 발견했다고 해서 그것이 반드시 참이라는 뜻은 아닙니다. 수많은 계산에서 같은 결과가 나왔다고 해도 아직 확인하지 못한 예외가 존재할 수 있습니다. 특정 조건에서 성립하는 관계가 모든 경우에 성립한다고 단정할 수도 없습니다.

패턴을 발견하는 것과 수학적으로 증명하는 것은 다르기 때문입니다.

바로 이 지점에서 Lean이 등장합니다.

Lean은 수학적 명제와 증명을 컴퓨터가 검증할 수 있는 형식으로 표현하는 정형 증명 보조 도구입니다. 사람이 제시한 증명 과정이 정해진 논리 규칙에 따라 올바르게 이어지는지 확인합니다.

비유하자면 AI가 복잡한 미로에서 새로운 길을 탐색하는 역할이라면, Lean은 그 길이 실제로 출발점에서 목적지까지 이어지는지 논리적으로 확인하는 역할에 가깝습니다.

물론 Lean도 한계가 있습니다. 잘못된 명제를 형식화하거나 부적절한 가정을 설정했다면, Lean이 그 명제 자체의 현실적 의미까지 보장해 주는 것은 아닙니다. 형식화된 전제 안에서 증명이 올바른지를 검증하는 것이 핵심입니다.

이러한 협력은 양-밀 이론과 같은 난제에서 더욱 중요해집니다.

4차원 양-밀 양자장론을 엄밀하게 구성하고 질량 간극이 존재한다는 사실을 증명하려면 방대한 수학적 구조와 정교한 논리가 필요합니다. AI는 기존 연구를 분석하고 새로운 증명 전략을 탐색하는 데 기여할 수 있으며, Lean은 형식화된 증명의 논리적 정확성을 확인할 수 있습니다.

여기서 우리가 주목해야 할 것은 AI가 인간을 대신해 수학을 완성한다는 이야기가 아닙니다.

발견과 검증이라는 서로 다른 과정을 연결함으로써 인간이 도전할 수 있는 수학의 범위를 넓힐 가능성입니다.

무리수의 존재를 증명하고, 무한의 크기를 구분하며, 자연의 힘을 수학적 구조로 표현해 온 인류의 여정은 이제 새로운 도구와 함께 다음 단계로 나아가고 있습니다.

AI가 가능성을 제시하고 Lean이 논리를 검증한다면, 인간은 그 과정에서 무엇을 질문하고 어떤 방향으로 나아갈지 결정합니다.

그렇다면 언젠가 AI와 Lean의 협력은 양-밀 이론의 오랜 수수께끼까지 해결할 수 있을까요?

Covid was the great awakening, and I'm not sure the people running the system have fully grasped it.

The globalists. Brussels. Macron. Everyone who thought they were managing a crisis.

Before Covid, a lot of people were asleep. They didn't see how insane the system had become. They didn't see how badly part of the elite wanted to take individual freedom away, one "temporary" measure at a time.

Then Covid came, and that camp showed its true face. Control everything. Regulate everything. Decide who can work, who can travel, who can see their family, who can walk into a restaurant. Not a single policy. A reflex.

Call it fascist, call it communist, it's the same thing underneath: a small group convinced it has the right to centrally plan human lives.

So here's a short message to them, on behalf of humanity.

People will be ready to die to keep their freedom. They always have been. That's what all of history says.

Your project won't work. Even if you managed to build your Orwellian state, it would only be temporary. Because even the people inside it, the ones who woke up, would look around one day and say: this isn't normal. And they would bring it down from the inside. Every centralized system that tried to cage human beings ended that way.

And honestly, it's fine. Everyone makes mistakes. You've been making them for 30, 40 years. Your worldview is wrong, it's abject, and it has failed every time it's been tried.

So change course.

Give individual freedoms back to everyone. Trust entrepreneurs. Trust human genius. Trust people to run their own lives.

And stop believing you're going to manage humanity like cattle.

x.name: Brivael Le Pogam
x.text:
We blame capitalism and overconsumption for what's happening to the planet. But I think some humans on this Earth do far more damage than even the most excessive consumption ever could.

Steve Jobs said it best: Bill Gates has no taste. Absolutely no taste.

And honestly, I think that sums it up.

Taste isn't about fonts or design. Taste is understanding humans. Knowing what they want, what moves them, what they'll never accept. It's the one thing you can't compute.

Gates never had it. He sees the world as a computer system. Humanity is a network. Populations are nodes. Behavior is code. Find the bug, push the patch, deploy at scale.

It works for Windows. It doesn't work for 8 billion people.

Because when you start from false assumptions about human nature, you end up doing crazy things. Very rationally. Very methodically. With billions of dollars behind you.

Watch him talk about Covid. He's still surprised it "didn't work the way he expected." He thought a pandemic would galvanize everyone. In his model, people would be grateful to be protected. Lockdowns, mandates, passes: optimal patch, rational users, problem solved.

Except humans aren't users. They want to be free. They'll take risk over control. They'll push back the moment they feel managed like a fleet of machines.

Every civilization that lasted understood this. Gates never did.

And the scary part is that the same man, with the same model of humanity, now wants a say in how we govern AI. In how we live with superintelligence. The most important decision of our species, made by someone who still hasn't figured out why people didn't want to be patched.

That's what dangerous looks like. Not malice. A worldview with zero taste and unlimited resources.

The world will be better off the day people like Bill Gates lose their grip on decisions that belong to all of us.

x.name: Brivael Le Pogam
x.text:
For months now, Bill Gates has been sounding the alarm on AI.

His latest warning: AI-powered cyberattacks will be the big story of the next 12 months. Bad actors stripping the safeguards out of models. Self-regulation isn't enough. Governments need to step in.

The diagnosis isn't crazy. Cyberattacks will explode. I build with these models every day, I know exactly what they can do.

But watch where the solution leads.

Oversight. Mandatory safeguards. Monitoring. Then, inevitably: licenses. Approved labs. Compliance bodies. A whole peripheral economy of bureaucrats whose job is to decide who has the right to run intelligence and who doesn't.

"Is your model authorized?"

That's the wrong answer. And a dangerous one.

Here's the thing about cyberattacks: attackers will have the models anyway. Criminal groups and hostile states don't apply for licenses. Regulation doesn't disarm them. It only disarms everyone else.

The only real defense is to go faster. Accelerate open source AI so that every company, every developer, every sysadmin on earth has the best models to audit their code, find vulnerabilities before attackers do, patch at machine speed and harden every system we depend on.

Security has always worked this way. Open source code is more secure, not less, because a million eyes are on it. Same thing for intelligence.

Will there be a phase of chaos? Yes. There will be one no matter what. The only question is whether we go through it with defenses spread across all of humanity, or concentrated in the hands of a few approved actors.

I'd rather take the risk of moving very fast toward an open superintelligence available to everyone than let a small group of enlightened people decide what life with superintelligence will look like for 8 billion humans.

And in my experience, people who see themselves as enlightened are usually enlightened about their own interests.

This is exactly the debate that gave birth to OpenAI.

A couple of years before its founding, Elon Musk had a conversation with Larry Page about the future of AI. Elon defended humanity's place in that future. Page called him a "speciesist." For being pro-human.

Then Google bought DeepMind. Elon realized the most powerful technology ever created was heading into the hands of one company, run by people who weren't particularly attached to humanity.

So in 2015 he co-founded OpenAI. The name said it all: an open AI, for humanity, not owned by a small group.

We know how that story ended.

Today we're back at the crossroads.

Path one: Gates wins. And he pulls the same move he pulled with software.

In 1976, a young Bill Gates wrote his "Open Letter to Hobbyists," attacking people who freely shared software. Twenty-five years later, Microsoft's CEO called Linux a "cancer." The entire Microsoft playbook was taking something that should be a commodity and putting a toll booth on it.

Except this time the toll booth won't be a license key. It'll be the law. Regulation as a moat. Coercion dressed up as safety.

Path two: AI goes fully open. Intelligence becomes infrastructure, like electricity, like the internet, like Linux, which now runs most of the world's servers.

And when intelligence is infrastructure, the winners aren't the ones who lobbied best in Washington or Brussels. They're the best builders.

That's the world I want. Not one where you need permission to think.

Open source won the server. It won the internet. It must win intelligence. https://t.co/NM477YPqaj

정부의 적극적인 주택신속공급 정책으로 부동산 가격이 하향 안정 지표를 그리고 있습니다.

국토부가 잡아낸 레전드 부정청약 수법

로또 청약 한 번 당첨되면 수억 원 시세차익이 생기니까, 사람들의 잔머리가 범죄 영화 수준으로 진화함

국토부가 병원 진료기록과 직장·월세 내역까지 탈탈 털어서 잡아낸 실제 사례들임

1. 고소득 의사 부부의 허위 퇴사 → 직후 재입사
- 돈 잘 버는 의사 부부가 '저소득층 신혼부부 특별공급' 자격을 따내려고, 입주자 모집공고 바로 전날 병원에서 퇴사 처리해 무소득자로 둔갑한 뒤 공고가 나자마자 다시 재입사해 당첨됐다가 덜미가 잡힘

2. 결혼해 애까지 키우면서 서류상 남남인 위장미혼
- 인천 아파트와 분양권을 가진 2주택자와 버젓이 결혼식 올리고 애까지 낳아 같이 살면서, 무주택 추첨제 당첨되려고 혼인신고만 안 하고 버티다 적발됨

3. 같은 아파트 단지 사는 장인 집으로 부인만 전입신고
- 남편과 아내는 한집에 살면서 서류상으로만 아내 주소를 같은 단지 장인 집으로 옮겨 장인을 부양가족에 끼워 넣고 가점을 뻥튀기함. 심지어 공장·창고·모텔로 주소를 옮긴 사례도 수두룩함

이런 편법 당첨자 때문에 정직하게 청약통장 부으며 기다리던 무주택 실수요자 내 집 마련 기회를 도둑맞은 셈임

적발되면 '계약 취소 + 분양가 10% 계약금 몰수 + 징역 3년·10년 청약 금지'
- 예전엔 주민등록등본만 봤지만 이제는 부모님의 동네 병원·약국 결제 내역과 자녀 출퇴근 기록까지 교차 검증해서 다 잡아내는 중임

앞으로는 서류 한 장으로 끝나는 게 아니라 의료·통신·신용카드 빅데이터로 실거주를 상시 검증하는 시스템이 들어가서, 어설픈 위장전입이나 편법은 계약금 수천만~수억 원만 날리는 자충수가 될 거임

x.name: Matt Cole
x.text:
Bitcoin fell 19% into the biggest IPO ever. Now it's down 18% heading into the second biggest.

SpaceX raised $75B when it went public on June 12. In the 50 days before it listed, Bitcoin dropped 19%. Anthropic plans to raise up to $64B when it lists next week, and Bitcoin is down 18% over the same stretch. Overlay the two and they look almost the same.

What happened after the SpaceX IPO is the notable part. Bitcoin bottomed 18 days after the listing, then recovered all the way. By Day 100, it was above where it started.

Bitcoin around the SpaceX IPO:

Day -50 to IPO day: -19%
Low (Day +18): -25%
Day +50: still -20%
Around Day +70: a sharp rally
Day +100: +3.7%

From the IPO-day close to Day +100, Bitcoin gained 28%. From the low, it gained 39%.

The takeaway is that the selling came in the run-up to the listing. The bottom had effectively happened by the IPO, and the recovery came relatively shortly after, and it came all at once.

If Anthropic follows the same pattern, most of the drawdown is behind us, and it could reverse quickly over the next couple of months. And Bitcoin is sitting right at its 200-week moving average.

Map the SpaceX path onto today's price and you get roughly $90k by late February. Markets rarely follow a comparison like this exactly. But we remain very constructive on both the technicals and the fundamentals heading into 2027, and it's not hard to imagine what the narrative would be if anything close to this plays out.

x.name: Brivael Le Pogam
x.text:
Haiti just ran the cleanest A/B test of the century.

Option A: the international system. Thirteen years of UN peacekeeping, billions in aid, an army of NGOs. Result: a president assassinated in his own bedroom, a capital run by gangs, more than a million people displaced. The peacekeepers themselves brought cholera to the island and killed nearly 10,000 Haitians. After the 2010 earthquake, the Red Cross raised half a billion dollars and built six permanent homes. Six. Oxfam staff were caught paying for sex workers in the ruins.

Option B: Bukele. A few weeks, 2,000 soldiers, armored vehicles, one clear objective. Result: the gangs are now writing letters to the UN asking for "mediation."

Read that again. The gangs are asking the UN to protect them. They know exactly who is a threat to them and who isn't.

This isn't about Haiti. It's about the operating system the West has been running since the 60s, and it is dying in front of us. Its axioms were wrong.

Axiom one: everyone can be reinserted, the criminal is a victim of the system, punishment is oppression. El Salvador tried truces and soft approaches and became the murder capital of the world. Then it stopped believing it.

Axiom two: force is always illegitimate. But order isn't natural. It's built and maintained, sometimes by force. A state that refuses to use legitimate violence doesn't abolish violence. It hands the monopoly to whoever is willing to use it. In Haiti, that's the gangs.

Axiom three: everything can be steered from the top. Central banks, planners, aid agencies, "development" programs. Decades of money pushed down from above, and the result is always the same: a class that lives off the problem and has zero incentive to solve it. An NGO that fixes Haiti loses its budget. Think about that.

Axiom four: morality is relative and the old norms were just oppression. This one was built by a very specific elite in the 60s and 70s. In 1977, Sartre, Beauvoir, Barthes, Deleuze and others signed a petition in Le Monde defending sex between adults and minors. Those people are the intellectual grandparents of today's ruling class. Epstein isn't an anomaly. He's the tail of that comet: a network of untouchables who believed rules were for other people.

Now the system is cornered, and it has two exits.

Exit one: lock everything down. Digital IDs, programmable money, censorship sold as safety, a technological control state more total than anything Orwell imagined. Keep the bureaucracy, add the surveillance.

Exit two: let it collapse and rebuild on what actually works. Individual responsibility. Freedom. Consent. Clear rules, actually enforced. Decentralized systems that emerge from the bottom instead of central planners who are never accountable for their failures.

Haiti just showed us which one delivers.

The 20th century bet on the bureaucrat. The 21st belongs to builders, and to states that do what they say.

x.name: Brivael Le Pogam
x.text:
🚨 Ursula von der Leyen, Emmanuel Macron, the WEF crowd and the whole globalist class are building a Europe where you will not be free to think and not be free to speak. 🚨

Here's the principle they've forgotten. In the field of ideas, freedom means everything gets said, even the most abject things. They must be said, and then they must be fought, in the open, with arguments. That's the only way a society learns where the line actually belongs.

And here's why the European Union, as it's built today, can only produce one thing: people afraid to say what they believe is right and wrong.

The EU runs on a simple belief. An enlightened elite, technocrats nobody really elected, supposedly knows better than 450 million people what is true, what can be said and what must be removed. Once you believe that, you need tools to enforce it. And brick by brick, they're building them: a digital cage for the human mind.

Look at the pieces.

Chat Control is a law to scan private messages in the name of protecting children. In March 2026, the European Parliament voted to kill the temporary version. By July, it was back in force through a procedural threshold, even though more MEPs voted against it than for it. It now runs until 2028. The permanent version, whose original draft would have made scanning mandatory, is still being negotiated behind closed doors.

The DSA hands Brussels the power to police illegal content, "systemic risks" and disinformation on the platforms where you speak. Its first fine landed on X, the one major platform openly at war with Brussels' vision of moderation. The official reason was blue checkmarks and transparency. Every other platform got the message.

The digital euro: in July 2026, Parliament voted to open negotiations, with a pilot planned for 2027. They promise privacy. But once your money is issued and tracked by a central authority, the infrastructure for control exists. Promises change with governments. Infrastructure stays.

And then there's Macron, touring France to warn about social media and pushing for a label to tell you which news sources deserve your trust.

Every piece comes with a noble reason: protect children, fight disinformation, ensure security. Nobody builds a cage by calling it a cage.

Here's the fundamental mistake. Truth doesn't come from the top. It never has.

Truth emerges from the whole network. It comes from millions of nodes: people who see something wrong, find the courage to say it, get attacked, hold on, and end up being proven right. It's the same reason central planning fails in economics. No committee holds the knowledge that is scattered across an entire society. Hayek showed this about prices. It's just as true about ideas.

History is full of abject consensus certified by experts.

In 1941, Joseph Kennedy had his 23-year-old daughter Rosemary, JFK's sister, lobotomized. Doctors told him it would calm her mood swings. She had been sneaking out of her convent school. The surgery destroyed her. She spent the rest of her life institutionalized, unable to speak properly. And this wasn't fringe medicine. Eight years later, the inventor of the lobotomy received the Nobel Prize.

Now imagine a Ministry of Truth in 1941. Who gets flagged for "medical disinformation"? The doctors performing lobotomies, or the people screaming that it was barbaric?

That's exactly what's at stake today. There's a strong chance that one day, what we are doing to children in the name of gender transition will be remembered as one of those abject consensuses. Maybe I'm wrong. But the only way to find out is to be allowed to question it. A system that freezes what can and can't be said turns its errors into permanent ones.

If you can't challenge the status quo, you are not free. You are the subject of an abject bureaucratic system that decides on your behalf what you're allowed to think.

Peter Thiel saw this long ago. In his lectures on the Antichrist, he argues that the real danger isn't the catastrophe itself. It's the one-world system that rises by promising to save us from it. Its slogan, he says, is "peace and safety." Fear of Armageddon becomes the justification for total control. He calls it his one departure from classical liberalism.

That's the trap. They sell you protection from the apocalypse, and the cage is the apocalypse.

And this is where everything I've written about fear comes together. A system built this way can only produce fear. Fear of being flagged, of being labeled, of losing your account, your job, your reputation. A society afraid to speak stops thinking. Then it stops creating. Then it dies.

So say what you think. Debate abject ideas instead of banning them. Defend the right of people you disagree with to speak, because it's the same right that protects you.

Truth has never come from Brussels. It comes from people brave enough to say it.

x.name: Brivael Le Pogam
x.text:
Elon Musk: "Look fear straight in the eye, and it will disappear."

His explanation is simple: the nature of fear is that people don't look at it. Look at it directly, and it's gone.

And this comes from a man who admits he feels fear quite strongly. He gave SpaceX less than a 10% chance of success. He started it anyway. Feeling fear is normal. Letting fear make your decisions is the mistake.

Now look around you.

Most people I know are afraid. Afraid of putting themselves out there. Afraid of looking stupid. Afraid of shocking their family at the dinner table. Afraid of being called racist for saying something they believe is true. Afraid of putting their relationship at risk. Afraid of their boss, their colleagues, their group chat, their neighbor. Always afraid of something.

And fear doesn't just stop you from acting. It shrinks you mentally.

When you're afraid, you stop thinking certain thoughts, because thinking them would mean you might have to say them. You start editing yourself before you even speak. Then before you even think. After a few years, you can't tell your real opinions from the ones that feel safe. You've become a negotiator between yourself and everyone else's judgment, and you always lose.

That's why fearful people almost never do anything. Not because they lack ideas. They have plenty. But every idea goes through the same filter: what will people think? And almost nothing gets through.

The project stays in a notebook. The company never gets started. The post stays in drafts. The conversation that would have changed everything never happens. Ten years go by and they tell themselves they were "being reasonable."

They weren't being reasonable. They were afraid.

So here's the only thing you need to tell yourself if you want to move forward in life: fear will never go away on its own. Waiting until you feel ready is waiting forever. You have to do exactly what Musk says: look it straight in the eye, name it, and act against it. Every single time.

Each time you do something despite fear, it loses a bit of its grip. Each time you give in, it gets stronger. Fear works like a muscle you're training. The only question is whether you're training your courage or your submission.

Musk's other trick is fatalism. Accept the worst case up front, accept that you might fail, and fear loses most of its power. What's left is the work.

The people who changed the world were not fearless. They felt the same fear you do. They just refused to let it hold the pen.

Fear doesn't make you careful. It makes you average.

x.text:
Intelligence is not what separated the great founders of the last 40 years from everyone else.

The world is full of brilliant people. Most of them never built anything that mattered.

The real difference is courage. The courage to say what you believe is true, knowing that 90% of people, sometimes more, will tell you you're wrong.

Jobs telling the world that normal people would want a computer at home. Bezos selling books on the internet while analysts laughed at his losses. Musk saying rockets would land and fly again while the whole aerospace industry called it a fantasy. Airbnb pitching strangers sleeping in strangers' beds. Every one of these ideas looked stupid before it looked obvious.

Thiel's question sums it up: what important truth do very few people agree with you on? Answering it is not an IQ test. It's a courage test.

And here's what fascinates me. Children have this courage naturally. A five-year-old asks "why?" fifty times a day. He says out loud that the emperor has no clothes. He doesn't care what people think of him. He hasn't learned yet that being wrong in public is supposed to be shameful.

Then he goes to school.

For fifteen years, he learns the opposite. Raise your hand. Give the expected answer. Repeat the lesson. Don't stand out. The grade rewards agreeing with what the teacher already believes. Fear of other people's judgment gets installed layer by layer until it becomes a reflex.

I'm pretty convinced the fundamental culprit is the left's capture of the school system. Not because teachers are bad people, but because an ideology that sees itself as the moral side of history has no reason to train kids to question it. It trains them to hold the right opinions. And a generation trained to hold opinions is a generation that can't produce new ones.

Now imagine the opposite. Schools whose explicit mission is to challenge the status quo, permanently. Where you score points for finding the flaw in the textbook. Where defending an unpopular position with rigor is the highest form of excellence. You would produce free thinkers.

And here's the uncomfortable part. Put free thinkers in a room and Marxism doesn't survive. Structurally. Not because of a rival ideology, but because it doesn't hold up under rational scrutiny. Central planning requires a planner to know what millions of people want, need and can produce. That information only exists scattered across their heads, and it only surfaces through prices. Hayek explained this decades ago, and every attempt since has confirmed it. An idea that only survives as long as nobody questions it is not a theory. It's a catechism.

Either way, we won't have a choice.

AI is wiping out the value of the pure executor. The person who learns the lesson and repeats it, applies the procedure, gives the expected answer: that is exactly what a model does better, faster and for almost nothing. Our education system was built to mass-produce that profile. That profile is now worth zero.

What will matter is people who know how to learn how to learn. People who face a problem nobody has solved and don't wait for the answer key. People who create things that didn't exist yesterday. And all of it starts with the same muscle: daring to think against the room.

So the real reform isn't coding classes or tablets in classrooms. It's tearing down the machine that kills the courage children are born with.

Children aren't afraid of being wrong. We teach them to be.

The future belongs to those who unlearn it.

x.name: Brivael Le Pogam
x.text:
If you want to succeed in life, read this.

Let's start with the truth nobody tells you at school: the system you're entering is deeply unfair and deeply unequal.

Some kids are born with everything. Parents who know the codes, the right schools, the network, the internships handed out over dinner. And some kids start with nothing. I'm the grandson of a Breton farmer. No network, no family name that opens doors, no diploma that impressed anyone. I taught myself to code at 12. Everything I have, I built.

So here's the first thing to understand. Money isn't distributed equally. Networks aren't. Connections aren't. But there's one weapon that's equally available to everyone, for free, from day one: courage.

And that's exactly what the system tries to take from you.

It doesn't keep people in line with force. It uses fear. Fear of looking stupid. Fear of disappointing your family. Fear of losing your job, your friends, your reputation. Fear of saying out loud what everyone thinks quietly.

Elon Musk put it better than anyone: "Look fear straight in the eye, and it will disappear." Fear survives because people refuse to look at it. The moment you stare at it, it shrinks.

Now let me name the fear you'll meet first.

The day you start speaking honestly about certain subjects, you'll be called racist. Not because you are. Because today, simply being economically right-wing is enough to earn the label. Believe in work, merit, lower taxes, free markets, borders, and someone will try to put that word on you.

Don't be afraid of it.

The word racist has been wrung dry. Real racism exists and it's disgusting, and that's precisely why the word used to be powerful. But a part of the left has turned it into a weapon to shut down debate, to weaken anyone who wants to say what they see. A word that applies to everyone ends up meaning nothing. And a weapon that no longer scares you no longer works.

So be driven by truth. Not by approval. Not by the fear of being labeled.

Steve Jobs told Stanford graduates not to be trapped by dogma, which he defined as living with the results of other people's thinking. And then he said the most important thing: "have the courage to follow your heart and intuition."

Your intuition already knows. You know, deep down, that the people fighting today, the ones being labeled far-right, are saying things that are true. You've seen it at school, at work, in your own city. You just haven't dared to say it yet.

And here's the good news: this fight is being won. The wall of fear is cracking. Every month, more people stop apologizing for what they think. Those who move first will be the ones who shape what comes next.

So stop asking permission. Stop waiting to feel ready. Stop negotiating with the fear of what others will think.

You didn't choose where you started. You choose whether you're afraid.

Free yourself from fear. And move.

x.name: Brivael Le Pogam
x.text:
For almost all of human history, the rule was simple: the majority crushes the minority.

The heretic at the stake. The Jew driven from town to town. The homosexual thrown in prison. Alan Turing, the man who broke Enigma and probably shortened the war by two years, convicted in 1952 for being gay, chemically castrated, dead two years later. A genius destroyed by the morality of the majority. One of the most shameful pages of the 20th century.

That tyranny was real. It had to end. And it is ending.

But history never moves in a straight line. It swings. After the war, and especially from the 70s on, the pendulum swung back the other way, and much too far.

Part of the intellectual elite of that era confused liberation with the destruction of every limit. Remember the 1977 petitions published in Le Monde and Libération, signed by the biggest names in French thought, calling for the decriminalization of sex between adults and children. The most admired thinkers in the country had lost all contact with reality. That wasn't freedom. It was decadence dressed up as the avant-garde.

From that matrix came an idea that ended up governing our institutions: the norm is suspect by nature, the majority is guilty by birth, and an enlightened vanguard has the right to rewrite the rules for everyone.

That's how we went from "let us exist" to "you will think like us." From protecting minorities to the tyranny of minorities.

DEI is the culmination of it. Hiring, promoting or excluding people based on skin color or gender, in the name of justice. Elon Musk put it bluntly: "Discrimination on the basis of race, which DEI does, is literally the definition of racism." You don't fix an injustice with a reverse injustice. You just create a new generation of resentment.

I think we'll look back on 1950-2030 as a parenthesis. A reaction, understandable after centuries of persecution, that ended up building a world designed for activist vanguards rather than for the majority of people who get up in the morning, go to work, raise their kids and simply want to be treated fairly.

And that parenthesis is closing. Not because one side won a culture war. Because reality always comes back. Ideologies that deny human nature always collapse under their own weight.

What comes next could be the best moment in human history.

For the first time, we'll have learned both lessons at once. That you don't persecute minorities: everyone is free to love who they want, believe what they want, live how they choose. Never another Turing. And that no minority, however well-intentioned, has the right to impose its worldview on everyone else.

No tyranny of the majority. No tyranny of the minority. Just free individuals, equal before the law, judged by what they do and not by what they are.

That's called humanism. And we're rediscovering it.

x.text:
11-13-26 A 10% Correction Is Still Possible — Here's How To Prepare

Markets are oversold, particularly in the technology sector, and November and December are historically among the strongest months for equities. But does that mean the bottom is in? Not necessarily.

While many growth stocks are starting to look attractive after significant declines, the current weakness could still develop into a broader 10% market correction. That's why patience, disciplined buying, and risk management are more important than trying to predict the exact bottom.

Here's how investors should approach this market:

1. Start Nibbling, Not Going All In
Oversold conditions create opportunities, but they don't guarantee an immediate rebound. Instead of buying an entire position at once, gradually build exposure as technical conditions improve.

For example, if you want a 4% portfolio allocation to $GOOGL, start with 1%. Add another 1% if the stock finds support and begins forming a base. Add more when MACD generates a buy signal, and complete the position if the stock breaks above resistance.

This approach allows you to participate in a recovery while preserving capital if prices fall further.

2. Rotate From Value Into Growth
Energy and other value-oriented stocks have enjoyed substantial rallies, while technology stocks have been beaten down.

Consider taking some profits in outperforming sectors and gradually reallocating toward oversold growth stocks. Rebalancing into weakness can position portfolios for a potential recovery without dramatically increasing overall risk.

3. Take Advantage of Higher Bond Yields
When Treasury yields spike, consider gradually adding duration to fixed-income portfolios. Higher yields can provide more attractive entry points, although longer-duration bonds remain vulnerable if rates continue rising.

4. Honor Your Stops and Manage Exposure
A 10% correction remains possible. Maintain stop-loss discipline, avoid oversized positions, rebalance on dips, and remain mindful of year-end tax considerations.

5. Don't Let Politics Drive Your Portfolio
Election results generate headlines and emotional reactions, but markets are already pricing in expectations about future policies.

Historically, stocks have tended to perform reasonably well after elections, although there are no guarantees. Investment decisions should be driven by earnings, fundamentals, technical conditions, and risk management rather than political predictions.

The bottom line: technology stocks are increasingly attractive, and favorable year-end seasonality could support a rebound. But the market may still have further to fall.

Don't chase the bounce or blindly buy the dip. Build positions gradually, rotate capital intelligently, protect your downside, and let the market confirm when it's time to become more aggressive.

Food for thought!

"High-Frequency Evidence on Post-Covid Treasury Yields and Bond-Stock Comovement" by Jing Zhou.

"Since mid-2021, long-term Treasury yields have risen by more than 300 basis points, and Treasuries have provided less offset to stock market losses. We study both changes in a single high-frequency framework that uniformly measures yield moves in narrow windows around major macro data releases, Treasury debt issuance announcements and auctions, and Federal Reserve monetary policy announcements, and we analyze the role of all three jointly. Before Covid, most of the movement in yields and of their comovement with stocks occur outside these windows. After Covid, both move into macro and debt issuance windows. Together, these windows occupy 4 percent of trading time but account for over 60 percent of the rise in the 10-year yield and most of the positive bond-stock comovement, more so at longer maturities."
